headline: The quiet stretch broke with an easy, unremarkable run — exactly the confirmation you wanted. Legs answered fresh, not flat. Ten days to a 580 km self-supported crossing.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The run back after the long pause did precisely what a run back should: sat controlled and low, mostly aerobic with only a brief touch above easy, at a pace that reads relaxed for you. That's the useful signal — the tempo effort and the week-long gap left the legs rested rather than dulled. Strength stayed live right through the pause, which is the answer to a question left open a couple of days ago; the maintenance thread held rather than going dark before departure. Steps remain high on training days, keeping the legs ticking with untracked bike commuting layered on top, though the rest-day zeros mean the daily-movement floor isn't uniform. Cardio load reads as detraining, but that's a mechanical artefact of a deliberately empty running window against a fuller 28-day base — not a fitness verdict. Recent four-week volume still sits well above the prior block, so the underlying trajectory is expansion recently reined in, not decline.
sections.trends: Year-to-date, you're running at more than four times last year's distance to this date — the medium-term shape is clearly a build, not a plateau, layered onto a strength base that has held its weekly rhythm for nearly two months. The recent taper-shaped dip is a local feature within that rising line, timed to the crossing rather than a change in direction. Given a goal of durable year-round hybrid capacity feeding into a multi-day self-supported effort, that shape makes sense: accumulate, then bank and rest before a sustained event.
sections.threshold: The threshold benchmark is a single early-July data point with no rolling baseline behind it yet, so treat it as a marker rather than a trend line. What the recent runs tell you more reliably is that easy aerobic pace is being held at comfortable heart rates — the engine is intact and responsive. For a 580 km trail effort, absolute threshold speed matters far less than the durability and controlled-aerobic economy the recent easy runs demonstrate. There's nothing here suggesting aerobic fitness has slipped during the pause.
sections.zones: The recent distribution is exactly what a taper into an ultra should look like: the return run sat almost entirely in easy-to-moderate territory with only a token minute higher, and most of the block's runs cluster in the low aerobic zones. The one deliberate exception was the fast session before the pause, which carried genuine time in the harder zones — a clean, isolated sharpening stimulus rather than grey-zone drift. That contrast between one hard day and the rest kept easy is the right pattern; the intensity hasn't leaked into the easy work.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions continue to run as low-intensity, largely Zone 1 work by heart rate — appropriate for functional maintenance rather than a cardiovascular hit, and consistent with the light-touch role strength is playing right now. The most recent few strength sessions logged without heart rate at all, so there's less to compare there. Nothing in the sensor-source pattern is out of step — the estimated and direct readings tell the same story of controlled effort.
sections.calendar: The rhythm here is a long unbroken running streak now paired with a strength habit that's held steady for weeks, and notably strength kept firing even through the deliberate running gap — the two threads don't collapse together when one goes quiet. That independence is a good sign of a genuinely multi-modal routine rather than a running schedule with lifting bolted on. The pattern to note as travel approaches is whether both threads can stay loosely alive through logistics without needing structure.
sections.personal_bests: No PB is in play here, and that's by design — the current block is durability and taper, not speed. Your short-distance bests were set last autumn in a sharpening phase; they're not the target of this window and won't be threatened by an ultra-oriented block. Revisit them when the calendar swings back toward speed work after the crossing.

watch_items: Watch whether strength stays as light maintenance or tapers to nothing in the final days before travel — either is fine, just note which way it breaks.
Watch that daily steps and movement don't collapse to rest-day zeros as logistics ramp, so the legs stay ticking rather than cold into departure.
Watch how the body handles the shift from short controlled runs to sustained daily time-on-feet once the crossing begins — the first days are the real durability test.
Keep an eye on sleep as travel and packing intensify, but read it as context only, not a readiness signal.
